subject.title: fix(agents): bound stalled SSH directory uploads with an idle watchdog

question: Should SSH sandbox setup impose a default 60-second deadline after the local archive closes, or should that post-producer limit be owned by a higher-level sandbox operation deadline with an explicit compatibility contract?
rationale: After the producer closes, the code cannot distinguish a genuinely stalled SSH session from a healthy but quiet remote extraction, so selecting a fixed default is an availability and compatibility policy decision rather than a purely mechanical timeout fix.

options.title: Use a caller-owned operation deadline
options.body: Retain the archive-stream no-progress watchdog and have the sandbox setup owner provide the post-producer cancellation policy, preserving existing long-running remote extraction behavior by default.

options.title: Adopt the 60-second default explicitly
options.body: Keep the fixed post-producer grace, document it as a supported sandbox-operation limit, and add real upgrade evidence for slow remote extraction and filesystem cases.

options.title: Pause the post-producer bound
options.body: Land only a solution that can prove a remote-progress signal or otherwise defer the post-producer hang case until its policy is agreed.

recommendation.title: Use a caller-owned operation deadline
recommendation.body: Retain the archive-stream no-progress watchdog and have the sandbox setup owner provide the post-producer cancellation policy, preserving existing long-running remote extraction behavior by default.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent SSH sandbox implementation history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the operational timeout contract.
